properties.project_name: P11A -- traffic median (half-circle island near Mission Bay Circle)
properties.digitized_from: Hand-traced from satellite imagery, guided directly by the owner's own marked-up screenshot (their drawn outline extracted from the photo via ORB feature-matching/homography rather than re-estimated by eye), then fit to an idealized semicircle per the owner's description of the real shape.
properties.digitization_method: ADDED 2026-09-19: resolves plan label P11A, previously only a weak ~33m proximity guess with no real source. The owner corrected this session's own repeated mis-location of the label (first a mis-anchored transform landing in the wrong intersection entirely, then a hand-eyeballed shape that didn't match) by drawing directly on a satellite screenshot. That drawing was extracted programmatically: ORB keypoint matching between the annotated photo and the original sent image gave a homography, chained through a second homography to a freshly-fetched satellite tile with an exact known lon/lat extent, so the owner's blue outline was converted to real coordinates without manual pixel-guessing. The owner then described the real shape as a half-circle; a circle was least-squares-fit to the arc portion of the extracted outline (radius 24.2m, fit residual std 0.58m) and a straight edge fit to the flat portion, then the two were combined into a true semicircle (flat edge through the circle center) rather than left as the noisier hand-traced outline. This is the grass median island immediately east of the roundabout named 'Mission Bay Circle' in this tracker (near P8/P10/X1), west of the Parklab Gardens soccer field. join_approximate.py --strict flagged a 28% MAJOR CLIP against the real street/curb buffer -- investigated rather than auto-accepted or blindly shrunk: the clip lands on the median's own top-left corner near the crosswalk, which DataSF's curb layer treats as street right-of-way (curb-return/crosswalk geometry legitimately overlapping a median island's edge, the same class of case documented for Pier 70's 20th Street Plaza). The owner granted an explicit exception rather than have the shape distorted to dodge the buffer -- street_clip_exempt set per that documented escape hatch, not used to silence a real mispositioning.
properties.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- owner-guided satellite trace, idealized to a fitted semicircle rather than left as a raw hand-traced outline. Not a surveyed footprint or GIS file from the project team. street_clip_exempt=true: this is a real traffic median, inherently adjacent to/overlapping the street right-of-way in DataSF's curb data at its crosswalk corner -- clipping it against the generic street buffer would cut a real, visible piece of the median, not a mispositioning artifact. Owner-approved exception.
properties.p_number: P11A. Not named in either neighboring Mission Bay Commons record's own p_number source (OCII's Nov 2024 CAC update only names P11/P12/P13/P15/P16/P17) -- resolved here by direct owner identification instead.
properties.notes: Traffic median island, landscaped with grass, immediately adjacent to a thin connector strip (P11) leading to the roundabout.
